prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2005 UK manifesto text (policy and record, stripped of ideological framing)

Record claimed since 1997
- Economy: Sustained growth, low inflation and interest rates, highest employment on record; over 2 million more in work; minimum wage and tax credits introduced; reduced absolute poverty among children and pensioners.
- Public services: Major funding increases; more teachers, support staff, doctors and nurses; shorter NHS waiting times; improved primary school results; reduced deaths from heart disease and cancer; crime down around 30%.
- Communities and borders: More police and Community Support Officers; faster asylum decisions; expanded international aid; early emissions trading to cut greenhouse gases.

Key proposals and targets
- Economy and work: Maintain low inflation target and fiscal rules; no rises in basic/top income tax rates; efficiency savings to fund frontline services; raise employment rate towards 80%; increase minimum wage as advised; reform incapacity benefits with work-focused support; back manufacturing, science and R&D (aim for 2.5% of GDP by 2014); streamline regulation; support SMEs and entrepreneurship.
- Transport: Over £180bn public investment to 2015; rail reliability and capacity upgrades, Crossrail solution, assess high-speed links; targeted motorway expansion and congestion management; examine national road pricing; free off-peak local bus travel for over-60s and disabled; safer roads and cleaner vehicles; include aviation in EU emissions trading.
- Energy and environment: Mixed energy strategy (renewables, nuclear, clean coal, microgeneration); climate targets of -20% CO2 by 2010 and -60% by 2050; Marine Act; stronger local environmental enforcement; expand recycling.
- Education: Personalised learning; guaranteed catch-up in basics; all secondary schools to be specialist; expansion of Academies (aim ≥200 by 2010) where standards are low; stronger discipline; more vocational routes and apprenticeships; Education Maintenance Allowances; expand FE reform; higher education funding with variable fees capped at £3,000, grants and bursaries; long-term goal of 50% participation.
- Health and care: Further reduce waits to a maximum of 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008; expand primary care, community hospitals, independent capacity at NHS standards; strengthen hygiene and MRSA controls; patient choice and information; integrate health and social care; school food and nutrition standards; tighter marketing to children; extend smoke-free places; expand cessation services.
- Crime and security: Neighbourhood policing team in every community; strengthen powers on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder; expand drugs testing and treatment; Serious Organised Crime Agency; tougher controls on weapons; offender management to cut reoffending; confiscate criminal assets; improve victim support; corporate manslaughter law.
- Migration and borders: Points-based migration system prioritising skills; English tests for settlement; employer penalties for illegal working; biometrics for visas and e-borders; phased ID cards linked to passports; streamline appeals; maintain obligations to refugees while tightening abuse controls.
- Older people: Pension Credit maintained and uprated to 2007–08; free off-peak local bus travel; long-term pensions settlement after commission review; right to request work beyond 65; pilot individual budgets for care; consider flexible working rights for carers.
- Families and housing: Halve child poverty by 2010 on the path to eradication; universal Sure Start Children’s Centres by 2010; extended schools offering childcare 8am–6pm; longer paid maternity leave (aim up to a year) and options for shared leave; widen homeownership (raise stamp duty threshold; shared ownership); increase social housing supply and quality.
- International: Active role in EU reform and global security; referendum on EU Constitutional Treaty; retain independent nuclear deterrent; UN reform; increase aid to 0.7% of national income by 2013; push for fairer trade rules and end to agricultural export subsidies by 2010; global action on climate change and communicable diseases.
- Culture, sport, media and digital: Free entry to national museums retained; broaden participation in arts and sport; improve facilities and school sport; support 2012 Olympic legacy; BBC governance reform via a new Trust; digital switchover by 2008–2012; modernise IP and support film production.
- Governance and devolution: Further devolution to nations, regions and cities; stronger local government with fewer funding streams and inspections; options for directly elected mayors; council tax restraint; House of Lords reform (remove remaining hereditary peers; time limits on bills; free vote on composition); Single Equality Act and a new equality/human rights commission.
